text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read, so other people can understand it quickly. One key idea is to follow good naming conventions. Use clear names for variables and functions, such as "totalPrice" instead of "tp". Another important point is to keep functions small and simple. Each function should do only one job. This makes your code easier to test and fix. Clean code is also easier to maintain. When you need to change something later, you can find the right place fast. In short, writing clean code saves time for everyone.
